classification.habit: Medium-sized evergreen tree with a dense crown and drooping young foliage.
classification.habitat: Shady moist evergreen forests and stream banks; widely planted in gardens and near temples.
classification.distribution: Central and Eastern Himalaya, Western Ghats, Eastern India and the Deccan; cultivated throughout India.

identification.description: Stem bark pieces are channelled or curved, with rough greyish-brown outer surface and reddish-brown inner surface; strongly astringent.
identification.whole_plant: Evergreen tree 6–9 m tall with dense dark green foliage; young leaves coppery-red and limp, hanging in tassels.
identification.stem: Trunk erect with dark brown to greyish, warty bark.
identification.leaf: Paripinnate, 15–25 cm long, with 4–6 pairs of oblong-lanceolate leaflets; young leaves reddish and drooping.
identification.flower: Fragrant, orange-yellow turning scarlet, in dense axillary corymbs; petals absent, calyx petaloid, stamens 7–8 and long-exserted.
identification.fruit: Flat, leathery, oblong pod 10–25 cm long, purplish-black when ripe, containing 4–8 seeds.
identification.bark: Channelled pieces, externally dark green to greenish grey with circular lenticels and transverse ridges; internally reddish-brown with fine longitudinal fibres; fracture splintery; taste astringent.
identification_points: Channelled bark, reddish-brown inside, with circular lenticels
Thin whitish layer below the cork
Splintery fracture and strongly astringent taste
Paripinnate leaves with drooping coppery young shoots
Orange to scarlet flower clusters without petals

therapeutics.precautions: Strongly astringent and may cause constipation. Heavy or irregular uterine bleeding should be diagnosed before treatment.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy except under specialist advice; avoid in Vibandha. Market bark is often substituted with Polyalthia longifolia, so authenticated material is essential.

अशोकः शीतलस्तिक्तो ग्राही वर्ण्यः कषायकः ।
दोषापचीतृषादाहकृमिशोषविषापहः ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The stem bark is rich in tannins and contains a crystalline glycoside, with catechins and flavonoids also reported.

modern_information.evidence_summary: A prime uterine tonic, it regulates menstruation and reduces cramps.
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated at classical doses; its astringency can cause constipation, and adulteration of commercial bark is common.
